chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

When you visit a sick person, say: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, from the evil of every swollen vein and from the evil of the heat of the Fire,' seven times.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when visiting a sick person in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi through the chain of Zurarah, a prominent companion of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith prescribes a specific dua for visiting the sick. The supplication invokes Allah as the Lord of the Great Throne to seek protection from the evil of every swollen vein and the heat of Hellfire, to be recited seven times. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of using specific prophetic and imamic supplications as spiritual remedies (ruqyah) during illness.
